steps.content: You stand on the lake's surface, alone and shadowless.
This is less a lake than a single slab of cool blue-green jade that time has forgotten. Nothing ripples here. Nothing reflects. An absolute stillness hangs in the air, inspiring dread.
At the far end stand two hollow doors, and from them emanates a soft, dreamlike glow.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: So this is her consciousness? A "lake" steeped in poison and time.
You walk toward the doors. White motes of light rise from your footsteps, coalescing before you into human-shaped phantoms—

steps.speaker: Mama
steps.content: Papa went fishing today. When he comes home, we'll make fish soup. The broth will be so white and good. Drink it all up, and you'll grow fair and strong, my little one.

steps.speaker: Mama
steps.content: Mama's sweet child... grow up healthy. Grow up beautiful. The prettiest girl in the whole village, you'll be.
The woman's features are blurred, but her gestures remain clear. She tucks a wildflower into the little girl's hair and gently smooths the strands the wind tousles.

steps.speaker: Mama
steps.content: Slow down, sweetheart! Don't fall now. Don't scar that pretty face.

steps.speaker: Mama
steps.content: Mama's precious girl... my Ayiguo... you have to live on. Beautiful and bright.
The little girl seems oblivious to her mother's words. Still laughing, she runs toward you, passes straight through your body, and dissolves back into falling motes of light.
You continue forward. The phantoms around you grow denser. The warm white light darkens without warning, turning heavy and oppressive. The scenes before you shift abruptly—

steps.speaker: Companion
steps.content: So many bugs! Snakes everywhere! Don't bite me! Get away, get away! Papa! Mama! Where are you?! It hurts!

steps.speaker: Companion
steps.content: Do you think we'll make it? I'm so scared... I don't want to die here. I want to go home...

steps.speaker: Companion
steps.content: Ayiguo... that's your name, right? That's good. You still remember your name...

steps.speaker: Companion
steps.content: Ayiguo... I don't want to die yet...

The pool of blood churns. Insects and snakes tear at flesh. The joyful little girl from the previous illusion plunges into the crimson depths. Blood and filth coat her face. Her skin rots and heals, only to rot again in an endless cycle. Her anguished screams and struggles give way slowly to numb stillness. Around her, companions come and go in waves.

Gradually, the venomous creatures lose their power over her. Her gaze grows dull, lifeless. Blood vessels burst and fade in her eyes, over and over, until at last they settle into a permanent crimson ring around each pupil.

The little girl stares at a wildflower blooming by the pool's edge, as if wondering how such beauty can exist in a place of blood. You reach out to her. Your hand passes through her phantom form as expected, dissolving into nothing.

At last, you pass through Ayiguo's fragmented memories, a century's worth, and arrive before the two doors. The scattered motes of white light coalesce into dozens of palm-sized paper figures. They encircle you.

steps.speaker: Paper Figures
steps.content: Boo-hoo, boo-hoo, the tears fall down. The weeping child can't be found. Seek and search, look all around. Two doors wait. Which way is sound?
You step closer and peer inside. Two auras churn within the doors, utterly opposed—a brilliant golden light that radiates from the left, and a pitch darkness that fills the right.
You rest your hand on the doorframe. The wood grain feels warm and solid beneath your palm. Inside, afternoon sunlight flows like honey, saturating the wooden cabin entirely.
Soup bubbles on the kitchen stove. A young couple busies themselves with cooking. White-haired Ayiguo sits in a woven bamboo chair, children nestled at her side, begging for stories.

steps.speaker: Elder Ayiguo
steps.content: Those adventure tales you love so much... they're all so far from us. This granny's lived a simple life. A happy one. To be ordinary... to grow old in peace... that's fate's greatest gift.
Golden sunlight traces her silhouette gently. Each wrinkle seems to hold a quiet contentment. The house is serene, beautiful, filled only with the soft echo of her peaceful voice...

You rest your hand on the doorframe. Inside lies a viscous darkness. Within a poison pool, venomous insects and serpents churn through bloody water. Ayiguo stands at its center in her youthful form, and with a casual crook of her fingers, countless creatures surge at her command.

steps.speaker: Monster Ayiguo
steps.content: Beauty. Power. Who wouldn't reach for them? Heehee... Now I'm a monster. This is right. This is how it should be.
The girl's whisper sends the poison pool into a sudden boil. Black shadows begin to creep outward, surging toward the doorway with the stench of decay...
[End of Branch]

You rest your hand on the doorframe. Inside lies a viscous darkness. Within a poison pool, venomous insects and serpents churn through bloody water. Ayiguo stands at its center in her youthful form, and with a casual crook of her fingers, countless creatures surge at her command.

steps.speaker: Monster Ayiguo
steps.content: Beauty. Power. Who wouldn't reach for them? Heehee... Now I'm a monster. This is right. This is how it should be.
The girl's whisper sends the poison pool into a sudden boil. Black shadows begin to creep outward, surging toward the doorway with the stench of decay...
You rest your hand on the doorframe. The wood grain feels warm and solid beneath your palm. Inside, afternoon sunlight flows like honey, saturating the wooden cabin entirely.
Soup bubbles on the kitchen stove. A young couple busies themselves with cooking. White-haired Ayiguo sits in a woven bamboo chair, children nestled at her side, begging for stories.

steps.speaker: Elder Ayiguo
steps.content: Those adventure tales you love so much... they're all so far from us. This granny's lived a simple life. A happy one. To be ordinary... to grow old in peace... that's fate's greatest gift.
Golden sunlight traces her silhouette gently. Each wrinkle seems to hold a quiet contentment. The house is serene, beautiful, filled only with the soft echo of her peaceful voice...
[End of Branch]

You pull your gaze away and step back, examining both doors. One is an illusory dream, the other reality... Or are both of them traps? Before you can think it through, the paper figures leap out and urge you onward.

steps.speaker: Paper Figures
steps.content: Boo-hoo, boo-hoo, the heart beats fast. The weeping child awaits at last. Left door, right door, choose your path!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What happens if I choose wrong?

steps.speaker: Paper Figures
steps.content: Choose right, go home tonight. Choose wrong, you're gone, swallowed whole!

The nursery rhyme grows shriller and shriller as the paper figures slap at you with insistence. You want more time to think, but the entire space begins to tremble violently. Beneath your feet, the jade-like surface of the lake splinters, delicate cracks spreading like ice about to fracture.

steps.speaker: Paper Figures
steps.content: Choose now! Choose now! The heart will break! The doors will close!
Your body screams with searing pain and suffocation. There is no time left to hesitate. You struggle toward the door on the left.

steps.speaker: Monster Ayiguo
steps.content: Little one, where are you going? This side is better, isn't it? Ayiguo will be here. She must be.
Your body screams with searing pain and suffocation. There is no time left to hesitate. You struggle toward the black door on the right.

steps.speaker: Elder Ayiguo
steps.content: To live an ordinary life as a normal person... isn't that the better dream? Ayiguo will be here. She must be.
A voice from the other door whispers in your ear. It tempts you. You hesitate, stop again. Your insides twist together, forcing you to double over in agony.
Even more irritating are the clamoring paper figures. They are fluttering, ramming into you from every side.

steps.speaker: Paper Figures
steps.content: Choose now! Choose now! The sky will fall! The earth will cave!

Your legs buckle beneath you. You sink to one knee on the lake surface, arms trembling as they barely hold you up. Then you see strange-colored patterns rising from your fingertips, a perfect mirror of those on Ayiguo's body. You freeze. Ayiguo did mention her wish before...

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Is it so wrong for a girl to want pretty things? To stroll down a sunny street, take in the noise and the bustle, feel alive without something chewing at her insides?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: You understand, don't you? This wanting to just... be normal?
You endure the pain of toxins corrupting your body and struggle toward the golden door, the one on the left.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But after gaining that much power... can anyone really settle for ordinary? After enduring pain like hers... can simple happiness ever be enough?
Just as you are about to step through the golden door, your feet stop once more. But... time is up.
CRASH!!!

The entire space shudders as though struck by a massive hammer. The jade-like lake surface shatters, sending debris flying in every direction. The paper figures are torn to shreds, their piercing shrieks echoing through the chaos. The door frames shake violently, and the glows within them begin to flicker as if they could slam shut at any moment.
The consciousness space is collapsing! There is no time left to overthink. You dive through the door just as it begins to fall apart—
(Scene change)
No sunlight reaches this place. There is only the viscous poison and the endless churning of insect carcasses.

Ayiguo lies in the pool, her body divided—half in bloom of youth, half in ruin. A network of spiderweb veins, purple-black in hue, maps her once-fair skin as the poison spreads through her with a will of its own. She takes no notice. She merely seizes a passing poisonous insect and consumes it without ceremony.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Buzzing bugs, behaving bugs... all fly into Granny's mouth!

Ayiguo licks the venom from her fingertips, and her laughter rises, sharp and growing. With a single swallow, the decayed half of her face begins to mend, the rot receding inch by inch as life creeps back into the flesh.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: That silly boy's been wandering in here an awfully long time... What, did he come all this way just to sightsee?
steps.female_content: That silly girl's been wandering in here an awfully long time... What, did she come all this way just to sightsee?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Ah, well. That illusion was so lovely, so warm and gentle. He'll choose it, surely. After all... this granny told him herself. "I just want an ordinary life."
steps.female_content: Ah, well. That illusion was so lovely, so warm and gentle. She'll choose it, surely. After all... this granny told her herself. "I just want an ordinary life."

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: "I won't believe a word you say"—wasn't that the line? And yet, when it mattered most... you still believed this wretched old liar's sincerity. Hahaha...

She raises her left hand and lets the venom cascade over her head. Wherever it flows, the poisonous scars fade into smoothness. Then she raises her right hand, and the wrinkles on her face vanish without a trace.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: People always say an ordinary life is what truly matters. That's only because they've never tasted what it's like to be a god.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: They fear me because I hold the power of life and death in my fingertips. They call me a monster draped in poisonous scars... But I'll stay young. Beautiful. Forever.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Being a villain is wonderful. Why can't anyone understand that? Ah... but I suppose the strong are destined for solitude. Expecting mere mortals to grasp such things... perhaps this granny asks too much.

The space beyond the poison pool collapses, and the water trembles in answer. At the entrance, the light flickers, threatening to seal the place shut at any moment. Ayiguo's smile falters for an instant as the thought of that person in gray crosses her mind. A fleeting shadow of regret passes over her face.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Sigh... It seems that little one isn't coming after all. This granny... really is going to rot away in here alone.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So this is how you stay young?
A voice cuts through the dark.
Ayiguo, who has been resting with eyes closed, opens them now. A glimmer of joy slips across her gaze, unfelt by her own awareness.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Oh? And here I was certain you'd choose poorly. Yet here you stand. Didn't you see the other door, little one?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: A perfectly safe path, right there for the taking. And instead you come barging into this old granny's poison den? Tired of breathing, are we?

You ignore the horrifying sights that surround you and the collapsing illusion beyond the door. You approach the poison pool. Along its edge, white and yellow wildflowers sway, the same ones you saw in the illusion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This pool is nothing but death. But flowers still grow here. You never forgot what your mother told you, did you? "You have to live on. Beautiful and bright."

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Ancient history. Who bothers remembering such things?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You remember. That's why you're torn in two. You want an ordinary life, but you know there's no road back to it.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I almost walked through that beautiful illusion. But then I realized it. I needed to know what you would choose. Not what I thought you wanted.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Oh? Reading minds now, are we? Go on, then. Let's hear this grand theory of yours.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Maybe you wanted ordinary once. A simple, quiet life. But after everything you've survived... you know that door's been closed for a long time.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You don't want someone to save you... You want to keep living, beautifully and freely. Without anyone's leash around your neck. That's why you'd never choose what's behind that other door.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Everything you've endured... it won't let you accept an ugly version of yourself. And it won't let you just lie down and die.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If you had another choice, you wouldn't want the shackles either. But this was the best answer you could find. You don't trust me, just as I don't trust you.
Ayiguo picks impatiently at her ear with her pinky, yet something flickers in the depths of her eyes.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: So what?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So we can work together. But first, you need to wake up.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're still inside the illusion. Your real body is out there, bleeding poison and Mania. The longer you stay here, the worse it gets. The more damage you take.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You wrapped yourself in that cocoon at the last second. I don't know how much longer it holds. When it breaks, and I suppose it will, the Mania and poison flood Eastside. The people there—
Before you can finish, the bloody water of the poison pool transforms into tentacles and sweeps you up into the air.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Work together? How precious. When this granny came to you with open hands, you turned me away. But now that you need something, here you are with pretty words and pleading eyes?

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: You think a few smooth sentences will make this old granny dance to your tune? Hah! You underestimate me, little one.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: What happens out there is none of my concern. I'm no upstanding citizen. I'm Granny Goldspider—capricious, immortal, a monster grown old.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: So what if they all perish? Those creatures who called me filthy. Cursed me as a freak. Prayed I'd rot away in some dark corner where they wouldn't have to look at me... Ignorant, small-minded fools, screeching their worthless noise. Not one of them is worth a single tear.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: What gave them the right... Who are they to judge me? Despise me? Drive me away? Call for my head like I was some rabid thing to be put down?
The people from her past and the fleeing figures of reality merge into one. Ayiguo's expression darkens, turning unreadable.

The bloody water of the poison pool suddenly boils. Ayiguo rises with it into the air, facing you down. Frenzied shadows whirl around her, carrying with them a swarm of venomous insects that buzz through the stagnant air.
A single venomous insect lands on the corner of your eye. Its sharp mouthparts emit a piercing shriek, a sound that echoes Ayiguo's seething bloodlust.

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: Kill him. Devour him. Take his power... and you will become the strongest being this world has ever known.
steps.female_content: Kill her. Devour her. Take her power... and you will become the strongest being this world has ever known.

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: Power without chains... Eternal youth and beauty... Wealth beyond measure... All yours.

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: This flesh you wear is nothing but morality's cage. Only through destruction can you be reborn.

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: You will never suffer again. Never be alone. Never be bound by their rules, their world, their scorn. You will be... free. Forever.
Shadows born of Mania seep from the poison pool and coil around Ayiguo. They whisper to her, tempting her toward surrender. You meet her gaze, finding her eyes now stained with darkness.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The flower is still blooming, Ayiguo.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It grows in a pool of blood because some part of you still wants to live. Not as a mindless monster, but as you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ayiguo, don't let Mania fool you. I've seen what happens to Sinners who give in. They become monsters, Corruptors.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Have you forgotten? You refuse to submit to any power, not even Mania! That's how you've survived everything thrown at you.

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: Ayiguo... You have no other road. Will you crawl back to your cage?!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There's a third road. I'll give you the shackles!

steps.speaker: Mania
steps.content: Have you forgotten?! Imprisoned. Controlled. Rejected. Cast out like a thing to be feared and buried!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then let's make a bet. You can master your poison and my shackles. Together, we find a way for you to live, not as a monster, not as a mortal. As something else entirely.
The shadows refuse to relent. They keep whispering in Ayiguo's ear.
Ayiguo lowers her head and says nothing. The silence stretches for long seconds. Then, abruptly, she leans forward, grabs hold of your collar, and drags you near.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Little one, do you understand what you're offering?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Can't be worse than what's already happening.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: If you lose this bet, my poison eats through you. Nothing left but a stain. And you still want to roll the dice?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I didn't walk in here expecting to walk out clean.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Hahaha! You are an interesting little thing! Just like this granny... a gambler to the marrow!

Ayiguo lets out a hearty laugh, loosens her grip on your collar, and steps away. The darkness drains from her eyes, her agitation ebbing by degrees. In you, she catches a glimpse of herself, someone willing to stare death in the face for the slimmest chance at life.
Beside her, Mania's shadow continues its ceaseless prattling. Ayiguo turns her head and spits a mouthful of poison its way. The shadow corrodes on contact and dissolves into nothing.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Enough yapping out of you, you overgrown pest!

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Well then. If you've got the stomach for it, let's give this a try.
Ayiguo stretches out her wrist toward you. The restraints that bind you fall away.
A blinding burst of red light erupts as the shackles activate. Before Ayiguo, a third door materializes into being.
(Scene change)
You gasp sharply and sit upright on the auction hall floor. A fit of violent coughing seizes you, and you spit up dark fluid laced with blood.
The spider silk that had swallowed the hall has vanished. The bystanders are evacuated. On the empty floor, Ayiguo lies curled in a fetal position, still shrouded in tattered remnants of silk.

You do not stop to assess your own wounds. You rush to her side and tear the poison-soaked silk away with your bare hands, uncovering her face. Her eyes are pressed shut. Your fingertips blacken swiftly on contact, then the next moment, the decay halts, suppressed by some invisible will.
Ayiguo's consciousness stirs. She is protecting you.
(Scene change)

Ayiguo stands in the fields of Eastia. Overhead, the sky opens wide and endless, clouds drifting lazily toward the horizon. A soft breeze moves through the grass and stirs the air around her. She cannot recall the last time such peace has settled upon her.

steps.speaker: Mama
steps.content: My precious girl, you have to live on. Beautiful and bright.

steps.speaker: Companion
steps.content: Do you think we'll make it?

steps.speaker: Passerby
steps.content: Monster! You're an undying monster!
Countless phantoms flicker at the edges of sight, appearing and dissolving like mist beneath the sun—present one moment, vanished the next.
Ayiguo watches with a strange fascination. She lowers her gaze to her own hands, clean and unmarked, and finds them unfamiliar.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: How lovely... to feel nothing at all.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: That little one was right. An ordinary life...? I lost the road back to that a long, long time ago.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: I clawed and killed and swallowed poison to survive like this. Not so I could wither away and die some pitiful death in a dark corner. Isn't that right?
The third door looms before her, sheathed in crimson spikes that coil like brambles and gleam like blades. But fear does not touch her.

She takes a step. From the ground, countless withered hands surge upward, clawing at her ankles, desperate to drag her back. She does not slow. Her stride, unwavering, tears through every grasping finger.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: My, my. What a heavy load this old granny's been hauling all these years. Give it a rest, won't you? Old friends. Old foes. Doesn't matter anymore.
The torn hands shift and flatten into paper figures. They link hands and form a ring around her, their voices rising in a nursery rhyme achingly familiar.
Little one who weeps, don't wander far. Round the world but never still. Steady stand the mountains tall, Clear and bright the waters fall...

Ayiguo inhales deeply. The air is laced with the faint, distant scent of her mother's steamed rice cakes. She steps across the threshold, and a warm red light, nearly searing, pours out and swallows her whole.
(Scene change)
A Few Days Later

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This is for you. Congratulations on being back among the living.
You place a small gift box on Ayiguo's bedside table, where it joins an assortment of snacks and flowers from other Sinners and staff members.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: A hair clip? Such a plain little thing. A single flower, no sparkle, no shine. Have you been living under a rock, <color=#fb9259>sweet pea</color>?
Sweet pea? Since when does this granny give you new nicknames?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's like the one you used to wear, isn't it? I used that as a guide. If it's not to your taste, I can swap it for something else.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Hey, hey! A gift given is a gift kept, no taking it back! Since you've shown proper respect to your elders, this granny supposes she'll hold onto it.
Afraid you might change your mind, Ayiguo quickly tucks the hair clip into her inner pocket, then lies back down with a contented smile.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: How are you feeling? You've been horizontal for days.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: This granny's right as rain. But you... you've got more nerve than sense. Weren't you the least bit worried about getting poisoned to death inside my cocoon?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You've been keeping poison on a leash for over a century. Mania's probably just another strong toxin as far as your body's concerned. And even if things went sideways, I'm the Bureau Chief. I would've managed.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: My, aren't we full of ourselves. Handed over the shackles without blinking. Not a single worry that this granny might turn the tables and use her poison to pull your strings?

options: What kind of Chief would I be if I get scared that easy?
Not at all. If I go down, you won't last long either.

choices.text: What kind of Chief would I be if I get scared that easy?
Not at all. If I go down, you won't last long either.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But that's a good point. I could use this chance to test how the shackles affect you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Anyway, we've both got something on the other now. If it came to blows, we'd both be scraping ourselves off the floor.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Bah! Bah! Such foul luck, always rattling on about death! This granny intends to live a thousand years in perfect health and beauty.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Then I'd better watch my step. I'll be counting on you to look out for me from now on. Stub my toe too hard, and those shackles might give you a little jolt in sympathy.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: What's that supposed to mean?! Making this granny your personal bodyguard? The nerve! Taking advantage of a poor old woman! Bullying your elders!

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: ...Still. I imagine more than a few eyes are on you. An elixir of immortality, walking around on two legs. Tempting target.

steps.speaker: Ayiguo
steps.content: Perhaps I should find a place nearby. Just to keep a proper eye on things. You, specifically.
